actions.action: Preserve item focus; define a removal destination
actions.mechanism: Stable product and control identities preserve focus through reordering; removed items send focus to the results heading.
actions.implementation: Key elements by product ID and control role. Before updating, capture focus. Restore only if disrupted; use a programmatically focusable results heading when removed.
actions.check: Reorder a retained focused product: the same control stays focused. Filter it out: focus reaches the heading. Filter controls retain focus.
actions.risk: Unconditional restoration can steal focus after the user moves elsewhere.

actions.action: Separate loading, count, and empty states
actions.mechanism: A persistent textual status exposes the latest count without moving focus; explicit loading text distinguishes pending results from zero.
actions.implementation: Keep status outside the busy results container. Show “Updating; previous count: N.” On arrival, update the visible count and polite live region within one second.
actions.check: Measure arrival-to-status latency. Test slow responses, zero matches, and nonzero matches with keyboard and screen reader; loading must never announce zero prematurely.
actions.risk: Assistive technology may delay speech despite timely live-region updates.

actions.action: Commit only the newest complete result update
actions.mechanism: Versioned, atomic updates prevent stale responses from reversing the count, item order, or focus destination.
actions.implementation: Assign each filter request a sequence number. Ignore older responses. Commit items, count, loading state, and the focus policy together for the latest request.
actions.check: Resolve two requests in reverse order. Only the latest appears. Repeat with a retained focused item and a removed one; verify the defined destinations.
actions.risk: Rejecting stale responses must not leave loading active after failure.

actions.action: Offer a compact view without hiding matches
actions.mechanism: Reducing card detail, rather than product coverage, gives users a less expansive way to browse the same results.
actions.implementation: Add a keyboard-operable compact-view toggle. Retain every matching product, its name, distinguishing variant labels, and details link; hide only supplementary previews.
actions.check: Compare product IDs and counts across views: they must match. Reach every details link by keyboard; verify variant distinctions remain readable without color.
actions.risk: Over-simplified labels can make distinct products indistinguishable; retain distinguishing information.
